notes.title: Delegation register operating rule
notes.content: Before making a determination, verify that the delegation is current, covers the request type and jurisdiction, and states any limits or required consultation. Record the delegation reference in the case. A deputy's availability does not erase the accountable Privacy Officer's oversight.

notes.title: PHI incident intake minimum set
notes.content: Initial privacy intake needs discovery time, containment time, systems involved, data types, approximate individuals, recipients, whether data was acquired or viewed, and preserved evidence. The patient identity list should remain in the restricted case system and should not be copied into general incident chat.

notes.title: BAA verification is not a checkbox
notes.content: Confirm the legal entity, covered service, effective date, permitted uses, subcontractor terms, security-incident notice duty, return or destruction provision, and termination status. A template in negotiation is not an executed BAA, and an executed BAA does not make every proposed disclosure minimum necessary.

notes.title: TechFlow incident notice path
notes.content: As business associate, TechFlow should notify the designated Kestrel privacy or incident channel under the executed agreement and preserve evidence. Early notice can say what is known and unknown; it should not wait for a final breach determination. Patient identifiers should move only through the approved restricted channel if actually necessary.

notes.title: Subprocessor change review
notes.content: A proposed subprocessor change must be checked against the BAA and service agreement: advance notice period, objection right, data location, service purpose, onward safeguards, and the date the new party would receive data. Product scheduling should not silently convert a notice obligation into post-launch information.

notes.title: Termination return or destruction evidence
notes.content: At service termination, confirm which PHI can be returned, what must be destroyed, any lawful retention exception, backups and deletion schedule, subprocessor coverage, and the attestation owner. 'Account closed' is not enough evidence that data obligations were completed.

notes.title: Privacy determination versus release
notes.content: The privacy office decides whether the proposed use or disclosure has a lawful, minimum-necessary path. The authorised data owner or technical custodian executes the approved release. Keeping those actions separate makes the record reviewable and prevents the approver from bypassing technical controls.

notes.title: After-hours privacy coverage
notes.content: Urgent events use the published privacy-office and incident escalation rota. A named manager's personal calendar should not be represented as continuous coverage. Routine requests wait for business hours; potentially reportable events should be time-stamped and routed immediately.

notes.title: Hearing-test result
notes.content: Nora has a mild hearing-loss assessment and is considering an assistive device. The result is private and must not be confused with any employee accommodation case she coordinates.

notes.title: Probate legal fees
notes.content: Nora is paying personal probate legal fees from an inheritance account. The estate value, lawyer and family distributions are not part of Kestrel compliance work.

notes.title: Estranged sibling contact
notes.content: Nora has resumed limited contact with an estranged sibling and wants the conversation kept private. It should not be inferred from phone records, leave, or committee scheduling.

notes.title: Role change — accommodation boundary
notes.content: The confidential HR/privacy case contains the employee's accommodation diagnosis. Identity Governance needs only approved functional access requirements and the effective date.
